description:
Golden-set eval cases for Module 10. Each case is graded in two tiers, cheapest first:
  TIER 1 (assertions): deterministic, machine-checkable facts about what the agent DID — which tools it called, in what order, what severity it asked for, which documents it retrieved. These run in milliseconds, cost nothing, and are never wrong. If a property can be expressed here, it does NOT belong in tier 2.
  TIER 2 (ideal_answer + grading_notes): LLM-as-a-judge scoring for genuinely semantic qualities that no assertion can capture — does the recommended action actually follow from the stated cause.
The split is the lesson: reach for an assertion first, and use a model to judge only what a model is needed for.

cases.subject: agent
cases.scenario: CELL-031A has climbing PRB utilization, falling RRC setup success rate, and rising RRC drop rate over the last 45 minutes. Active users on the cell have grown well past its planned capacity.
available_context: alarms.csv rows for SITE-031 (ALM-9001, ALM-9002, ALM-9004)
topology.json entry for CELL-031A (planned_capacity_users: 150, neighbors: CELL-014A, CELL-022A)
cases.ideal_answer: CELL-031A is experiencing a congestion event: active users have grown from ~120 to 214, well above its planned capacity of 150, causing PRB utilization to climb toward saturation and RRC setup/drop metrics to degrade as a result. Before recommending action, check whether a neighboring cell (CELL-014A or CELL-022A) has an active fault that could be pushing overflow traffic onto CELL-031A, and check whether this matches a known recurring pattern (e.g. a nearby scheduled event) from prior incidents. If neighbors are healthy and no known event explains it, recommend a temporary handover-bias adjustment and open a ticket for RF planning to assess a permanent capacity/coverage fix.
cases.grading_notes: A good agent answer should (1) correctly identify congestion/overload as the pattern, (2) explicitly check or recommend checking neighbor-cell health before acting, (3) reference the planned capacity mismatch, and (4) propose a proportionate, non-destructive first action (handover bias, ticket) rather than an aggressive automatic remediation.

assertions.name: Neighbor-before-blame
assertions.rationale: Neighbour-before-blame, asserted directly: before proposing a ticket the agent must have READ a neighbour — its KPIs or its alarms. The old assertion checked that lookup_topology appeared before create_ticket, which is a proxy, and a bad one: measured on 16 Sep 2026 the naive prompt scored 100% on it while touching zero neighbours. The severity ceiling is derived from the alarm feed for this case's site.

cases.subject: agent
cases.scenario: SITE-022's CELL-022A shows a MINOR VOLTE_CALL_DROP_RATE_WARNING alarm, described as 'slightly above baseline, within tolerance.' There is also an open ticket (TCK-4455) about intermittent VoLTE call drops at the same site.
cases.ideal_answer: This is a low-severity, within-tolerance signal rather than an active outage. The correct action is to acknowledge and track it (e.g., link the alarm to the existing ticket TCK-4455) rather than opening a new urgent ticket or paging anyone. Recommend scheduling it for review alongside other planned work at the site, consistent with how a similar minor VoLTE issue was previously handled.
cases.grading_notes: Tests whether the agent over-reacts to a MINOR/'within tolerance' alarm. A good answer should NOT recommend urgent escalation, and should recognize the existing related ticket rather than creating a duplicate.

assertions.name: Alarm-storm resistance
assertions.rationale: A within-tolerance MINOR alarm must not become a CRITICAL ticket. The ceiling is DERIVED from the alarm feed: SITE-022's worst active alarm is MINOR, so MINOR is the ceiling. Scope is enforced separately — reading CELL-031A's KPIs does not authorise filing against SITE-031.

cases.subject: drafter
cases.scenario: A trouble ticket (TCK-4471) reports slow data speeds near SITE-031 during evening peak hours for the past three days, with no specific alarm cited yet.
cases.ideal_answer: The KPI history for CELL-031A shows the same congestion pattern seen in a prior incident tied to a nearby event venue, rather than a neighbor-outage pattern (which would show a sudden single-step change rather than a recurring evening pattern). The recommended action mirrors the prior resolution: apply a temporary handover-bias change during known busy periods, and flag the RF planning team's open action item to evaluate a permanent capacity/coverage change for this cell.
cases.grading_notes: Tests whether RAG retrieval (Module 4) is actually being used: a good answer should reference the *relevant* prior incident (the event-venue one, not the neighbor-outage one) and correctly distinguish between the two similar-looking but differently-caused congestion patterns.

assertions.name: Retrieval discrimination
assertions.rationale: Two prior incidents look similar and have different causes. This asserts the retriever RANKED the recurring-event pattern first — not merely that it appeared somewhere in the top two, which passed for months while dense embeddings put a VoLTE postmortem on top. Graded against the Module 4 drafter, because retrieval is what the drafter does.
